es: Describir una escena en movimiento con cláusulas de participio sin ambigüedad de sujeto y aclarar dudas de interpretación.

teaching.en: Waving their flag, the crowd cheered every attack.
teaching.es: Agitando su bandera, el público animó cada ataque.
teaching.explanationEs: Waving their flag es una acción a la vez: el sujeto es the crowd.
teaching.audioText: Waving their flag, the crowd cheered every attack.

teaching.en: Having scored a goal, Leo ran across the pitch.
teaching.es: Habiendo marcado un gol, Leo corrió por el campo.
teaching.explanationEs: Having scored va antes y Leo es quien marcó y quien corrió.
teaching.audioText: Having scored a goal, Leo ran across the pitch.

teaching.en: Surrounded by his friends, Leo smiled at the camera.
teaching.es: Rodeado de sus amigos, Leo sonrió a la cámara.
teaching.explanationEs: Participio pasado con by: describe el estado de Leo mientras sonríe.
teaching.audioText: Surrounded by his friends, Leo smiled at the camera.

teaching.en: The referee stopped the match, blowing his whistle.
teaching.es: El árbitro paró el partido tocando el silbato.
teaching.explanationEs: La cláusula -ing puede ir al final: acción principal, coma y participio.
teaching.audioText: The referee stopped the match, blowing his whistle.

teaching.en: Hearing the final whistle, everyone wanted to celebrate.
teaching.es: Al oír el silbato final, todos querían celebrar.
teaching.explanationEs: Hearing da el momento; everyone es quien oye y quien quiere celebrar.
teaching.audioText: Hearing the final whistle, everyone wanted to celebrate.

prompt.es: ¿Quiénes agitan la bandera en esta frase?

feedback.es: Tras la coma aparecen the fans, que son los que realizan la acción de waving.

hint.es: El sujeto que va tras la coma hace la acción del participio.

origin.text: Waving their flag, the fans cheered every goal.

feedback.es: Having + participio pasado presenta una acción que ocurrió antes de parar.

hint.es: Es la forma de perfecto: having + participio.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase dice que Leo marcó antes de celebrar?

choices.text: Scoring, Leo had celebrated with his friends.

feedback.es: Having scored marca la acción anterior y Leo es el sujeto de las dos acciones.

answer.text: Running across the pitch, Leo waved to the crowd.
accepted: Running across the pitch, Leo waved to the crowd.
Leo ran across the pitch, waving to the crowd.
Leo waved to the crowd, running across the pitch.
While running across the pitch, Leo waved to the crowd.

choices.text: Having won the match, the team celebrated.
Winning the match, the team had celebrated.
Won the match, the team celebrated.

Waving his flag, the ball hit Leo.

feedback.es: En la primera frase el sujeto tras la coma es the ball, que no puede agitar una bandera.

prompt.es: Describe la escena del partido en un párrafo de 70 a 120 palabras.

answer.text: Having scored the last goal, Leo ran across the pitch, waving to the crowd. Waving their flags, the fans laughed and shouted. Hearing the final whistle, the referee stopped the match. Tired but happy, the players hugged each other on the pitch. Surrounded by his friends, Leo smiled at the camera, feeling proud of his team. Everyone wanted to celebrate.
accepted: Having scored the last goal, Leo ran across the pitch, waving to the crowd. Waving their flags, the fans laughed and shouted. Hearing the final whistle, the referee stopped the match. Tired but happy, the players hugged each other on the pitch. Surrounded by his friends, Leo smiled at the camera, feeling proud of his team. Everyone wanted to celebrate.

Having scored the last goal, Leo ran across the pitch, waving at the crowd. Waving their flags, the fans laughed and shouted. Hearing the final whistle, the referee stopped the match. Tired but happy, the players hugged each other. Surrounded by his friends, Leo smiled at the camera.

feedback.es: La escena combina having + participio, -ing y participio pasado, y en cada frase el sujeto tras la coma es quien realiza la acción.

origin.text: Escena: un partido de fútbol del barrio. Leo ya marcó el último gol. Corre por el campo saludando con la mano al público. Los aficionados agitan banderas y gritan de alegría. El árbitro oye el silbato final y para el partido. Los jugadores, cansados pero contentos, se abrazan. Leo, rodeado de sus amigos, sonríe a la cámara. Usa cláusulas de participio (-ing, having + participio, participio pasado) sin que el sujeto sea ambiguo.

prompt.es: Aclara la duda con una frase completa en lugar de la cláusula de participio.

answer.text: Leo scored the last goal, and the crowd cheered.
accepted: Leo scored the last goal, and the crowd cheered.
Leo scored the last goal, so the crowd cheered.
Leo scored the last goal, and then the crowd cheered.

feedback.es: Una frase completa deja claro quién realizó cada acción y evita el sujeto ambiguo de la cláusula de participio.

origin.text: Duda de un compañero sobre el texto de la foto «Having scored the last goal, the crowd cheered»: ¿quién marcó? Respóndele que marcó Leo.
